profile_text.body:
AssistiveWare describes itself as a builder of AAC, or Augmentative and Alternative Communication, apps, and as a sharer of best practices meant to help people communicate with the world. Its site frames that work around close collaboration with the AAC community and the idea that everyone has something to say. The site also carries educational material on AAC topics, including core words, Gestalt Language Processing, and a piece by support team member Lily Konyn, and it features the story of Jordyn Zimmerman, described as autistic and nonspeaking.

The company's tracked product is Proloquo2Go, listed under education and research AI, with word prediction as its AI feature. AssistiveWare describes it for students with communication needs and speech-language pathologists, and for users aged 2 and up, while the App Store age rating is 4+. On privacy, the vendor states usage data is collected anonymously, and the App Store label lists identifiers and usage data not linked to identity. No school account is needed. Pricing is $249.99 on the App Store, with an optional Gateway vocabulary at $149.99 as of May 2026.

The site also promotes a project called The Land of Autistic Communication, which invites visitors to explore forms of expression, and notes that one of its map locations, the Mountains of Echolalia, was animated this year.
